reason: I want to secure the first specimen for the journey, and the flight specimen locker is its natural destination.
expectation: I expect the membrane to be placed in the locker, completing or advancing the goal of bringing it home.

alternatives.reason: Harvesting lettuce would address the garden goal, but I want to stow the specimen first.

effect: Placing the membrane in the flight locker completed the specimen goal, leaving the garden goal.
reaction: It was a straightforward, reassuring way to secure the first specimen.
reason: The only available combination uses the scissors on the lettuce trough, which seems like the natural way to take some of the garden aboard.
expectation: I expect to harvest the new lettuce leaves for the flight galley.

effect: The scissors produced departure lettuce leaves, ready to take to the flight galley.
reaction: The harvest was straightforward; the result adds no further detail yet.
reason: The flight galley is the natural destination for the leaves, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the leaves to be prepared or stored for the journey, completing the garden goal.

effect: The leaves became a meal for the flight, completing the garden goal and bringing the chapter to departure.
reaction: The meal box and the plain falling away made the departure feel tangible; I was curious about what comes next.

mostWorthwhile.text: Putting the first specimen in the flight locker was most worthwhile because it secured the original find for the journey alongside the frozen core.

leastWorthwhile.text: Cutting the lettuce was the least engaging action: it was the only available combination, and its result added no detail on its own.

surprise.text: I was surprised that preparing the lettuce meal also led directly to liftoff; I expected it to complete the garden goal but did not anticipate the departure sequence.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary. The locker, scissors and galley each had a clear purpose, though the choices were mostly straightforward.

continue.text: Yes. The departure leaves me curious about the journey and what the receiving laboratory might learn from the specimens, even though this chapter offered few meaningful decisions.
